feature: An agent draws a picture and redlines a screenshot
summary: An agent session with the Photonz MCP server can now build a picture out of real layers (shapes, paths, text, Library components), place the Measure tool's own Size, Gap and Distance measurements on a screenshot, and export PNG or SVG. Every call is one undo step and leaves an ordinary layer you can edit by hand.
setup: Photonz Probe (or Dev, once rebuilt), release Next, no switch changed from its default. Server installed once with Scripts/install-mcp.sh (--probe for the probe). Both runs, call by call: 2026-10-19-agent-drawing-transcript.md.

try.do: In a new Claude Code session with the server, ask: Create a product icon svg of a box inside of a cloud.
try.shotNote: This is the exported SVG file drawn by Quick Look, not by Photonz; the file itself is 2026-10-19-agent-drawing-1-cloud-box-icon.svg.

try.do: Open the new Untitled window in Photonz: the tile, cloud and box are ten named layers. Click one and change its colour by hand.
Press Command Z a few times: each takes back one thing the agent did.
Open a UI screenshot in Photonz.
try.shotNote: Photographed with the window behind another app, the way a walk leaves it. Blue buttons and picked controls show their background look here; with the window in front they take the accent colour.

try.do: In a new session ask: annotate the ux with measurements around the major ui elements.
try.shotNote: Photographed with the window behind another app, the way a walk leaves it. Blue buttons and picked controls show their background look here; with the window in front they take the accent colour.

try.do: Pick any of the agent's measurements and drag a handle: it is the Measure tool's own redline and listed under Measurements.

evaluate: Is the icon from the one sentence prompt something you would start from, or does it need a house look the agent should be taught first?
On the redlined screenshot, are these the measurements you would have placed yourself, and is 13 about the right number?
The agent hid three of its own measurements whose numbers crowded others, rather than deleting them. Would you rather it deleted them?
Should text an agent sets skip the soft legibility shadow by default, as an icon wants, rather than only when asked?
rough: No mock covers this surface: it has no window of its own; the pictures are the probe window and the exported file.

Scenario 3, the run pictured: 13 measurements, 11 of them wholly on edges the picture really has (34 of 36 sides and feet within 3 px of an edge in the Measure tool's own edge map). The two partial: a page margin whose left end is the picture's border, and a 20 px distance whose lower end sits on empty background beside the buttons. Every number matches what a Size click reads on the same element.

Readouts still crowd round the top right switch and the fields in the pictured run. After it, the agent's Size now steers round the same neighbours a click does (the drawn layers and the elements as far out as a number travels), which moved the switch's width number off the next switch (2026-10-19-agent-drawing-5-switch-size-readouts.png, the app's own render). The run pictured predates that change.
The cloud is four white shapes, not one outline: combine_shapes would join them, and the agent was told so in the tool's description after this run.

Two earlier redline runs went worse and led to fixes in this task: one floated distances beside the elements with their ends on nothing (5 of 13 on edges), one read the text fields as 218 x 25 (their inner border) where Size reads 220 x 26.
find_elements takes about two seconds on a 1440 x 960 screenshot. Nothing in either scenario needed a capability the app lacks, so no prerequisite task was filed.
